items.text: Oil prices have surged again following the Iran war, with the ECB lifting rates for the second time since the conflict broke out. WTI and Brent crude are up ~5% and ~9% respectively. Eurozone inflation accelerated to 3.3% in August, its highest level in three years and well above the ECB's 2% target. For credit investors: commodity-linked refinancing risk and inflation sensitivity of consumer/small-cap debt is acute.

U.S. consumer sentiment fell to 51.7 in August 2026, a ~6% decline from July and roughly 11% below its year-ago level, reflecting persistent inflation concerns. Claims at 206k remain tame (4.1% unemployment), but September sentiment plummeted to a preliminary 47.8, with one-year inflation expectations jumping to 4.6%. Labor demand is holding but consumer distress is deepening—watch for layoffs if sentiment triggers demand destruction.

ECB deposit rate increased to 2.50% in September from 2.25% in August 2026. The 10-2 curve flattened 8bp to 33bp (already inverted on other measures). With PPI +5.41% and core PCE +2.45%, the Fed faces stagflation-lite pressure: growth-oriented credits face sustained duration headwind, while spreads may widen if recession fears intensify.

HY OAS tightened 2bp to 270, but CCC OAS widened 15bp to 1070, signaling widening quality dispersion. IG spreads roughly flat at 80bp. Curve inversion + elevated volatility (VIX 17.84, +3.5pts) create refinancing & covenant risk asymmetry: weak credit at risk, while stronger names can refinance or call.

China's official manufacturing PMI rose to 49.8 in August 2026 from 49.2 in July, but remained below the 50 threshold for a second consecutive month, signaling continued deteriorating manufacturing sector conditions. U.S. GDP Now tracker at 4.4% (way above actual 1.5% Q2 print) relies on unsustained momentum. Special situations investors should watch for cyclical credit stress and M&A opportunities in distressed sectors.

Retail sales (ex-autos) grew 5.75% YoY in July, moderating from 6.86%, while housing starts (1.24M) and existing home sales (3.98M) are both sliding. Mortgage rates at 6.76%. Policy uncertainty and the Iran conflict fuel gasoline price concerns, while consumers increasingly worry about weakening economic conditions, with one-year business expectations falling 10%. Consumer durable & housing credit face demand risk despite strong payroll beats (likely seasonal/statistical blips given July timing).

S&P 500 implied vol (VIX 17.84) elevated amid rate volatility and geopolitical premia, but not yet panic levels. Curve compression, oil shock, and sentiment collapse are broadening credit dispersion. Event risk: FOMC 15–16 Sept (inflation expectations now critical), plus potential further supply-chain/tariff surprises from Middle East conflict.

themeCards.title: Iran War Energy Shock
themeCards.statusLine: The ECB raised rates by 25bp at its September meeting, marking its second hike since the US-Iran war began, citing Middle East conflict as fueling inflationary pressures. Oil up ~5% WTI, ~9% Brent in recent days; downstream cost pass-through underway.
themeCards.relevance: Refinancing risk for energy-dependent credit & input-cost-sensitive issuers (consumer staples, autos, transport). Spreads in commodity hedgers & levered energy plays may blow out if oil stabilizes higher; refinancing windows closing for weaker credit.

themeCards.title: Consumer Sentiment Collapse
themeCards.statusLine: Consumer sentiment drops to 47.8 as gas prices and trade tensions push inflation expectations to 4.6%. August final print already showed 51.7 (lowest in cycle), but September preliminary is sharper cliff; lower/older cohorts distressed.
themeCards.relevance: Demand destruction risk for discretionary retail, restaurants, automotive. Consumer credit fundamentals at risk of rapid deterioration; ABS and auto loan securities vulnerable if sentiment translates to charge-offs within 1-2 quarters.

themeCards.title: China Manufacturing Contraction Spread
themeCards.statusLine: China PMI 49.8, below 50 for second month; output and new orders returned to expansionary, but employment continued to contract. Non-manufacturing PMI 49.0 (contraction). Small firm PMI still weak at 47.9.
themeCards.relevance: Spillover risk to credit exposure in EM, Asia-linked supply chain credit, and USD-denominated CHN corporates. May signal weaker global demand ahead; commodity & export-linked credit (metals, chemicals, machinery) at risk of margin compression and covenant pressure.

themeCards.title: Curve Inversion & Duration Trap
themeCards.statusLine: 10-2 spread collapsed to 33bp; 10-3M near zero or negative (not in FRED data, but inversion deeper than indicated). UST10Y +18bp to 4.95% in two days. Curve has inverted on short end for months.
themeCards.relevance: Non-bank borrowers funding long-term projects at short rates face rollover risk; floating-rate credit spreads may expand as terminal rates stay higher longer. Refinancing calendar stress for coupons maturing in 2026-2027; credit with step-ups or call optionality benefits.

themeCards.title: Quality Bifurcation in Credit
themeCards.statusLine: HY OAS 270 (tight) vs. CCC OAS 1070 (+15bp 1d). IG OAS 80bp roughly stable. Dispersion widening. Default risk concentrated in lower tier.
themeCards.relevance: High-yield sponsors with refinancing needs face maturity walls; CCC cohort (leverage, energy, small-cap retail) faces acute stress in high-rate environment. Distressed-for-value opportunities in high-conviction name selection; avoid broad HY longs.

themeCards.title: Fed Hike Expectations Resetting
themeCards.statusLine: Markets now pricing third ECB hike by December. U.S. CPI due today (Sept 11); PPI hot at +5.41% (aug data, +0.61% m/m surprise). Core PCE 2.45% but up 8bp from prior. Fed decision 15-16 Sept expected to stay on hold or clarify forward guidance.
themeCards.relevance: If inflation fails to roll over, Fed terminal rate expectations may re-anchor higher, pressuring long-dated credit spreads and triggering refinancing cascades. Credit dispersion likely to widen further as market reprices terminal rate above current market consensus.

ecb.delta: Hiked 25bp on Sept 10; second hike since Iran war

chinaPMI.delta: August official PMI, +0.6pts m/m but still below 50; contraction persists

ismServices.delta: August services PMI, +1.3pts from 54.1; 26 consecutive months in expansion

retailSales.delta: July ex-autos retail sales YoY; down from +6.86% prior, moderating

existingHome.delta: August existing home sales SAAR; down from 4.06M; housing stress widening

consensus.CPI: Headline ~3.2-3.4% YoY; Core ~2.4-2.5% YoY exp (last print 3.35% / 2.45%); today Sept 11 print expected
consensus.PCE: Core PCE 2.45% YoY (last print July); expectations for Sept TBD, latest August 3.7% headline, 3.34% core
consensus.PPI: August +5.41% YoY (latest available); Headline +0.61% m/m surprise high; consensus ~5.0% YoY exp
consensus.Retail Sales: Latest July +5.75% YoY ex-autos; August retail sales (ex-autos) not yet available, due mid-Sept
consensus.ISM Mfg: August 54.6 (actual vs. consensus 55.2 expected); September TBD, due Oct 1
consensus.ISM Services: August 55.4 (actual, beat 54.2 consensus); September TBD, due Oct 3
consensus.GDP: Q2 2026 +1.5% annualized (latest); GDPNow 4.4% (current tracker, reflects July data)

regime.label: Stagflation-lite, Inversion & Bifurcation
regime.detail: Sticky goods inflation (PPI high), energy shock, tight spreads vs. widening lower-tier OAS, consumer distress, inverted curve; Fed likely on hold or hiking into recession risk.
